plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous tree that covers its bare branches in clouds of pale pink-white, lightly almond-scented blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic cherry of hanami festivals and is widely planted in parks and along waterways.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate cities worldwide
plants.funFact: The cherry trees around Washington D.C.'s Tidal Basin were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom is tracked closely each year, often falling in late March.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with a trumpet-shaped yellow corona surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands, meadows, and grassy banks and has produced countless garden cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids such as lycorine, and one of its compounds, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large Himalayan tree that produces enormous, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in early spring. The blooms can reach 25 cm across and appear in rich shades of pink to deep rose.
plants.location: Himalayan foothills (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China) and cultivated in mild gardens in Britain, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Seedling trees of this species can take 20 years or more to flower for the first time, which is why gardeners often joke that patience is the main requirement for growing it.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.commonName: Autumn Crocus (Southern Hemisphere cultivated relatives) and Cyclamen hederifolium
